intended_object: A natural isomorphism, induced by a chosen basis `b` of V, between two functors on commutative K-algebras. The first is R ↦ End_R(V ⊗ R) as an additive group, with the tensor factors in source order. The second is R ↦ the R-points of the vector-group scheme of i×i matrices. I inferred this from the docstring ("The same comparison followed by the existing native matrix points") and from the surrounding definitions.
explanation:
The definition just composes two isomorphisms the library already has: `sourceOrderedEndMatrixGroupIso` (End to the additive matrix functor, through the basis) and `matrixGroupPointsIso` (the additive matrix functor to the points of the matrix vector-group scheme). It is glue that moves between the library's own models of the same functor: a tensor-order convention, a functor of additive groups, and a functor of scheme points.

It does contain the standard fact that a basis gives End(V)_a ≅ 𝔾_a^{n²}, but the declaration itself is a bookkeeping comparison between internal encodings, not a standalone mathematical notion that has a literature definition to check against. Nothing in it is mathematically wrong. The composite is well-typed, and the definition matches its docstring.
